nodes.label: AbstractListPayloadSplitter<T>
nodes.rationale: Collapses a full splitter to the one thing that differs per use case — the slice key — by fixing T=List<T>, R=T and supplying working defaults for splitIntoSlices, keyArgsToRecover and mergeSlices.

nodes.label: AbstractPayloadSplitter<T, R>
nodes.rationale: For a wrapper composite rather than a bare List: you implement splitIntoSlices to unwrap and mergeSlices to re-wrap, but still skip the context plumbing.

nodes.label: Slice-key contract (keyArgsForSlice vs keyArgsToRecover)
nodes.rationale: Store-side and recover-side args must derive the same store key for the same entity; if they diverge a slice is stored under one key and looked up under another and recovery silently returns nothing. This is why CSV tokens must be parsed to the stored key type (Long, not String), and why filters are excluded from the key so the entity can be shared across methods in a domain.

nodes.label: Defensive arg reading in keyArgsToRecover / splitOnRecover
nodes.rationale: Blind args.get(0) or casts throw on empty/null/wrong-typed args and then the splitter fails for every recovery; guard with the instanceof pattern and return an empty list, which the framework treats as 'no slices' (warn + skip) rather than an error.

nodes.label: Merge null policy (positional / compact / reject)
nodes.source_location: ## Partial Recovery: Null Policy in merge
nodes.rationale: Slices arrive in the same order splitOnRecover emitted them, so position carries meaning. Option A keeps nulls positionally when the caller maps results back by index, Option B compacts when the caller just wants what is available, Option C returns null on any miss when a partial list is unsafe. A cache miss, an expired entry and a timed-out slice are indistinguishable at merge — all null.

nodes.label: Splitter failures stay inside the failover boundary
nodes.source_location: ## Splitter failures stay inside the failover boundary
nodes.rationale: On the store path the exception is logged at ERROR and the real business result is returned unchanged, so a splitter bug never breaks a working upstream call; on the recover path recovery yields null and flows to RecoveredPayloadHandler and the ExceptionPolicy as a normal non-recovery. Users write no try/catch.
